title: Decir vs Hablar: Say, Tell, Speak or Talk in Spanish?
seo_title: Decir vs Hablar: Say, Tell, Speak or Talk in Spanish?

body_html:
Decir vs hablar is a pair where English has four verbs, say, tell, speak and talk, and Spanish has two. The key: decir focuses on what is said, the words or the message. Hablar focuses on the activity of speaking or talking. Me dijo que venía (He told me he was coming) reports content; Hablamos durante horas (We talked for hours) describes the activity. Add contar for telling stories, and you have the full picture.

Quick answer
  • Decir = to say, to tell (content): Dice que tiene frío.
  • Hablar = to speak, to talk (activity): Hablo con mi madre cada día.
  • Languages use hablar: Hablo español.
  • Stories, jokes and events use contar: Cuéntame qué pasó.
{{toc}}

Decir vs hablar: the core rule

DecirHablar
FocusThe words, the messageThe act of speaking
Englishsay, tellspeak, talk
Typical patternsdecir que…, decir algo a alguienhablar con, hablar de / sobre
ExampleDime la verdad. Tell me the truth.Tenemos que hablar. We need to talk.

The RAE dictionary defines decir as expressing thoughts with words, while hablar is the act of articulating words to communicate.

When to use decir

  • Reporting speech: Dijo que llegaría tarde. She said she’d be late.
  • Telling someone something: Te digo un secreto. I’ll tell you a secret.
  • Asking for words: ¿Cómo se dice “window” en español? How do you say “window” in Spanish?
  • Telling someone to do something: Me dijo que esperara. He told me to wait (subjunctive).
  • Opinions: ¿Qué dices tú? What do you say?

When to use hablar

  • Talking with someone: Hablé con el jefe. I talked to the boss.
  • Talking about something: Siempre habla de fútbol. He always talks about soccer.
  • Languages: ¿Hablas inglés? Do you speak English?
  • Manner of speaking: Habla muy rápido. She speaks very fast.
  • Being on speaking terms: No se hablan desde hace años. They haven’t spoken for years.
{{image:2}}

Contar: telling stories and news

English “tell” is often contar, not decir, when it means narrating:

  • Cuéntame cómo fue el viaje. Tell me how the trip went.
  • Mi abuelo cuenta historias increíbles. My grandfather tells amazing stories.
  • ¿Te cuento un chiste? Shall I tell you a joke?

Use decir for a short message or fact; use contar for a story or an account of events.

{{book:the-mind-lies}}

Useful expressions

  • Es decir… That is to say…
  • ¡No me digas! No way! / You don’t say!
  • Querer decir: to mean. ¿Qué quiere decir esto?
  • ¡Ni hablar! No way! / Out of the question!
  • Hablando de… Speaking of…
  • Dicho y hecho. No sooner said than done.

Conjugation note

Decir is very irregular: present digo, dices, dice; preterite dije, dijiste, dijo, dijeron (not dijieron); participle dicho; command di (dime); future diré. Hablar is a model regular verb. Contar changes o → ue: cuento, cuentas.

A quick mental shortcut

If you can put the words in quotation marks, use decir: Dijo: “Ya voy”. If you are describing who talked, with whom, about what or in which language, use hablar. If it is a story with a beginning and an end, use contar.

Real conversations

  • A: ¿Hablaste con Pablo? (Did you talk to Pablo?)
  • B: Sí, y me dijo que no puede venir. (Yes, and he told me he can’t come.)
  • A: ¿Por qué? ¡Cuéntamelo todo! (Why? Tell me everything!)
  • B: Es que habla muy bajito por teléfono y no entendí bien. (He talks really quietly on the phone and I didn’t catch it all.)

Why this pair is tricky for learners

English splits the territory differently: “say” and “tell” both report words, and “speak” and “talk” both describe the activity, but “tell” can also mean narrate. Spanish draws the line between message and activity, then gives storytelling its own verb. That is why learners often say dime una historia (from “tell me a story”) or hablé que (from “I talked that”). In my translation work, I check every “tell” in an English text and ask whether it introduces a message (decir), a story (contar) or an instruction (decir que + subjunctive). That single question fixes most errors.

Try it yourself

  1. What did she say? (¿Qué dijo?)
  2. We talked about the trip. (Hablamos del viaje.)
  3. Tell me what happened. (Cuéntame qué pasó.)
  4. He speaks three languages. (Habla tres idiomas.)
  5. What does this word mean? (¿Qué quiere decir esta palabra?)

Similar splits happen with {{link:pedir-vs-preguntar|pedir vs preguntar}}. For every pair, see {{link:spanish-confusing-words|my complete list of Spanish confusing words}}.

{{quiz}}

Final thoughts

The words: decir. The activity: hablar. The story: contar. Keep those three anchors and you’ll say, tell, speak and talk correctly in Spanish.

faq.q: What is the difference between decir and hablar?
faq.a: Decir means to say or tell and focuses on the words or message. Hablar means to speak or talk and focuses on the activity, who you talk to, about what or in which language.

faq.q: How do you say “tell me a story” in Spanish?
faq.a: Cuéntame una historia. Telling stories uses contar, not decir.

faq.q: Is it hablar con or hablar a?
faq.a: Hablar con: Hablé con mi jefe (I talked to my boss). Hablar a is used mainly for addressing an audience.
